bibl.title: Building Bridges: AI Custom Chatbots as Mediators between Mathematics and Physics

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: The results demonstrated that while AI-generated materials had an indefinite impact on learning outcomes, they significantly enhanced positive-activating emotions, situational interest, and self-efficacy, while reducing intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load.

span.label: learning with AI-generated explanations of proportional relationships
span.quote: The study assesses the impact of AI-generated learning materials on the learning experiences and performance of sixthgrade students, with a particular focus on proportional relationships in mathematical and physical contexts.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: The randomized controlled study with N = 214 students compared traditional textbook materials with explanations generated by a custom chatbot.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The chatbot's encouraging, motivating tone raises situational interest relative to neutral textbook prose
span.quote: One potential explanation for this outcome is the nature of the custom chatbot's tone, which is designed to be encouraging and motivating.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Accessible, conversational, human-like wording in the AI explanation lowers the processing demands of the material and so reduces cognitive load
span.quote: One to potential explanation for this outcome is the use of accessible language and a conversational and humanlike tone in the chatbot's responses.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Encouraging tone and/or the lowered cognitive load raise students' confidence that they can solve the task themselves
span.quote: A reason for this may be the encouraging tone of the AI-generated text or the reduced cognitive load, or a combination of both.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because students never used the chatbot themselves, individual learning difficulties were never diagnosed or addressed, blunting any performance effect
span.quote: It is possible that the lack of independent use of the chatbot in this study may have contributed to the observed outcomes, as it prevented the identification and addressing of individual learning difficulties.

span.label: Generalizability is limited by sample size, the snapshot implementation period, and the single topic and target group chosen.
span.note: what this limits: the generalisation of every result: THE SIZE OF THE SAMPLE AND THE BRIEF IMPLEMENTATION PERIOD (SNAPSHOT) AS WELL AS THE NECESSITY OF SELECTING A PA[rticular topic and group]
span.quote: The generalizability of the results is constrained by different factors: the size of the sample and the brief implementation period (snapshot) as well as the necessity of selecting a particular topic for a specific target group.

span.label: Materials were delivered centrally, so students never interacted with the chatbot themselves and individual differences in use could not be captured.
span.note: what this limits: what the intervention actually was: THE LEARNING MATERIALS WERE PROVIDED IN A CENTRALIZED MANNER, WHICH RESULTED IN THE LACK OF CONSIDERATION FOR INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES IN UTILIZATION - the students did not use the chatbot themselves
span.quote: Additionally, the learning materials were provided in a centralized manner, which resulted in the lack of consideration for individual differences in utilization and the potential for interaction with the chatbot.

span.label: The performance data are too thin to support a conclusion about learning outcomes.
span.note: what this limits: the learning-outcome question specifically: IT IS NOT POSSIBLE TO PROVIDE A DEFINITIVE ANSWER TO RQ5 BASED ON THE DATA COLLECTED IN THIS STUDY
span.quote: It is not possible to provide a definitive answer to RQ5 based on the data collected in this study.

span.label: The primary outcome did not move, and the conclusion says so plainly while the abstract calls the same result indefinite.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that AI-generated materials improve learning: the conclusion states no notable differences were identified in the performance test and that the influence remains unclear
span.quote: Nevertheless, the influence on learning outcomes remains unclear. No notable differences in the overall result of the performance test could be identified.

span.label: Generalisability is constrained by three named factors, including the brief period, which the authors themselves call a snapshot.
span.note: what this limits: extending these results to AI-generated materials in general: the authors name sample size, a brief implementation period they call a snapshot, and the particular topic and target group
span.quote: The generalizability of the results is constrained by different factors: the size of the sample and the brief implementation period (snapshot) as well as the necessity of selecting a particular topic for a specific target group.

span.label: The mechanism relied on to keep answers accurate is stated as a reduction in risk, not a guarantee.
span.note: what this limits: retrieval-augmented generation as a fix for factual error in these materials: the paper states it reduces the risk of hallucinations rather than removing it
span.quote: The reliance on external documents reduces the risk of hallucinations

span.label: instructing students who did not complete a task to select GUESS, so those responses are dropped from the evaluation
span.quote: In the interest of ensuring the integrity of the evaluation process, students who have not completed a task are instructed to select “guess” to exclude their responses from being considered during the subsequent evaluation.

span.label: custom chatbots
span.quote: The custom chatbots at OpenAI are designated as GPTs.

span.label: GPTs
span.quote: This is a relatively straightforward process for teachers or students to configure their own custom chatbots. The custom chatbots at OpenAI are designated as GPTs.

span.label: cognitive load
span.quote: The results demonstrated that while AI-generated materials had an indefinite impact on learning outcomes, they significantly enhanced positive-activating emotions, situational interest, and self-efficacy, while reducing intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load.

span.label: effect on learning outcomes - AS THE ABSTRACT PUTS IT: an indefinite impact, stated in the same sentence as the significant gains in emotion, interest and self-efficacy
span.quote: The results demonstrated that while AI-generated materials had an indefinite impact on learning outcomes, they significantly enhanced positive-activating emotions, situational interest, and self-efficacy, while reducing intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load.

span.label: effect on learning outcomes - AS THE CONCLUSION PUTS IT: no notable differences in the performance test, and the influence remains unclear
span.quote: Nevertheless, the influence on learning outcomes remains unclear. No notable differences in the overall result of the performance test could be identified.

span.label: custom chatbot - a configured instance of a vendor's LLM, which the paper notes OpenAI designates by a different name
span.quote: The custom chatbots at OpenAI are designated as GPTs.

span.label: replicates → previous research on emotions in chatbot-supported learning (reference [29])
span.quote: This finding is consistent with the results of previous research [29].

span.label: custom chatbots —same-as→ GPTs
span.quote: The custom chatbots at OpenAI are designated as GPTs.

span.label: Cronbach's alpha
span.quote: Cronbach's alpha was calculated for the purpose of evaluating the internal consistency of the individual scales

span.label: Shapiro-Wilk normality test
span.quote: Both the data of the EG and those of the CG were tested for normal distribution using the Shapiro-Wilk test with a significance level

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: To test for significant differences between the experimental and control group scores, the Mann-Whitney U test with significance level was used

span.label: effect size (Cohen's d)
span.quote: Cohen's d was calculated to estimate the effect size for significant differences

span.label: inter-rater reliability (weighted kappa)
span.quote: To ascertain the interrater reliability, Cohen's weighted kappa was computed for the two raters and for each category of the rating system

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: The average age of the students was 11.7 years (SD = 0.51).

span.label: mean
span.quote: The CG exhibits slightly superior mathematical performance (M = 2.24; SD = 0.88) than the EG (M = 2.38; SD = 0.95)

span.label: Sixth-graders who learned from a custom-chatbot-generated explanation reported more positive-activating emotions, more situational interest and higher self-efficacy, and lower intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load, than those who learned from textbook material, while learning outcomes showed no clear effect.
span.quote: The results demonstrated that while AI-generated materials had an indefinite impact on learning outcomes, they significantly enhanced positive-activating emotions, situational interest, and self-efficacy, while reducing intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load.

span.label: The two groups did not differ on the overall score of the performance test.
span.quote: No notable differences in the overall result of the performance test could be identified.

span.label: On two of the six table values in subtask B the textbook (control) group scored significantly higher than the AI-material group.
span.quote: For two values of task B (tabular), the CG demonstrated a significantly higher level of performance than the EG.

span.label: On subtask C, which asked students to calculate the constant of proportionality, the AI-material group scored significantly higher than the control group.
span.quote: Conversely, in subtask C, the EG performed significantly better.

span.label: The two groups were equivalent in prior interest in mathematics before the intervention.
span.quote: The data collected show no significant differences between the two groups in terms of interest in mathematics.

span.label: The reduction in cognitive load in the experimental group did not carry over into any measurable performance gain on the achievement test.
span.quote: Despite the fact that the experimental group exhibited a notable reduction in cognitive load, this did not translate into a statistically significant improvement in performance on the achievement test.

span.label: Large Language Models (LLMs)
span.quote: LLMs are a category of artificial intelligence based on neural networks, trained on vast datasets.

span.label: chatbots
span.quote: One of the most widely recognized applications of LLMs is in the field of chatbots, which are software tools that engage with the user in written dialogue [1].

span.label: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
span.quote: A way of augmentation is called Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) which is a method used to enhance and specify the capabilities of LLMs by integrating external data sources [42,43].

span.label: multiple representations
span.quote: Moreover, in the fields of physics and mathematics, comprehension problems potentially emerge from difficulties in interpreting and linking different forms of representation, which can be defined as multiple representations [19].

span.label: GPTs (OpenAI custom chatbots)
span.quote: The custom chatbots at OpenAI are designated as GPTs.

span.label: type of learning material (AI-generated explanation vs. textbook examples)
span.term: type of learning material (AI-generated explanation vs. textbook examples)
span.quote: The students were randomly assigned to either the experimental (EG) or the control group (CG).

span.label: conventional textbook material given to the control group
span.term: conventional textbook material given to the control group
span.quote: The CG was provided with conventional textbook material, comprising a topic overview and explanatory examples.

span.label: emotions during the learning phase
span.quote: Participants' emotions and situational interest were recorded.

span.label: situational interest
span.quote: Situational interest was measured with four items following the students' engagement with the learning materials.

span.label: intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load
span.quote: To measure the cognitive load during the learning process, a two-factorial model of cognitive load was used in this work, measuring intrinsic cognitive load (ICL) and extrinsic cognitive load (ECL).

span.label: self-efficacy expectation
span.quote: The self-efficacy expectation is evaluated in regard to the independent solving of a topic-related task on the basis of a scale comprising five items.

span.label: learning performance / transfer of mathematics into a physics context
span.term: learning performance / transfer of mathematics into a physics context
span.quote: Subsequently, in order to measure learning performance and the ability to transfer mathematical content to a physics context, the learners completed a performance test (see IV.A.6.) within 30 minutes.

span.label: learning time
span.quote: To ensure a fair comparison, the learning time was identical for both groups and amounted to 15 minutes.

span.label: medium of presentation (paper-based for both groups)
span.term: medium of presentation (paper-based for both groups)
span.quote: To eliminate potential bias caused by the use of digital media, both groups engaged in their studies exclusively with paper-based materials.

span.label: subject-specific interest in mathematics (baseline)
span.quote: Subject-specific interest was measured before the learning phase and served to examine the comparability of CG and EG.

span.label: N = 214 — number of sixth-grade German secondary-school students in the randomized controlled study
span.quote: A total of N = 214 sixth-grade students (146 female, 66 male, 2 n.a.) at secondary schools in Germany participated voluntarily in the randomized controlled study.

span.label: 11.7 years (SD = 0.51) — mean age of the participating students
span.quote: The average age of the students was 11.7 years (SD = 0.51).

span.label: 15 minutes — learning time allotted identically to both groups
span.quote: To ensure a fair comparison, the learning time was identical for both groups and amounted to 15 minutes.

span.label: 30 minutes — time allowed for the performance test measuring learning and transfer
span.quote: Subsequently, in order to measure learning performance and the ability to transfer mathematical content to a physics context, the learners completed a performance test (see IV.A.6.) within 30 minutes.

span.label: = 0.8469 — mean weighted-kappa inter-rater agreement across the rating categories for subtask D
span.quote: Computing the mean value of the interrater reliability from all categories, results in a mean value of kappa which indicates a very good degree of agreement between the two raters for = 0.8469

span.label: M = 2.24; SD = 0.88 vs M = 2.38; SD = 0.95 — last-term mathematics report-card grades of the control group versus the experimental group (German scale, 1 = best)
span.quote: The CG exhibits slightly superior mathematical performance (M = 2.24; SD = 0.88) than the EG (M = 2.38; SD = 0.95)

span.label: GPT-4.0 — the OpenAI base model the custom chatbot was configured on
span.quote: The chatbot was configured in multiple cycles based on the OpenAI GPT-4.0 model.
